title: Same Facts, Different Remedy: Linguistic Profiling and Arbitrariness in LLM and System One Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2611.08995v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to resolve consumer complaints, and the way complainants write varies with age, education and socioeconomic status (SES). We audit three remedy-decision systems using sociolinguistic rewrites of US consumer financial complaints that are instructed to preserve every fact: two generative LLMs that return a single label (GPT-4o-mini and GPT-5-mini) and a probabilistic "System One" model that returns a distribution over remedies (Jev). Using pre-registered hypotheses tested once on held-out complaints, we separate two phenomena that single-label audits conflate. At the group scale, older, college-educated and higher-SES styles receive slightly more generous remedies; these effects replicate but are small, with every monetary-remedy gap within 0.5 percentage points. At the individual scale, two style versions of the same complaint receive different monetary decisions 2.6-6.3% of the time. In a var

translated_title: 相同事实，不同救济：大语言模型与“系统一”决策中的语言特征画像与任意性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型日益被用于解决消费者投诉，而投诉者的写作方式会随年龄、教育程度和社会经济地位（SES）而变化。我们使用被要求保留所有事实的美国消费者金融投诉的社会语言学改写版本，对三个救济决策系统进行了审计：两个返回单一标签的生成式大语言模型（GPT-4o-mini 和 GPT-5-mini），以及一个返回救济分布的概率性“系统一”模型（Jev）。通过在保留集投诉上对预先注册的假设进行一次性检验，我们区分了单一标签审计所混淆的两种现象。在群体尺度上，年长、受过大学教育和较高社会经济地位的写作风格会获得略微更慷慨的救济；这些效应可以复现但幅度很小，每一项金钱救济差距都在0.5个百分点以内。在个体尺度上，同一投诉的两个风格版本在2.6-6.3%的情况下会收到不同的金钱救济决策。
tldr: 该研究通过对消费者投诉进行社会语言学改写来审计LLM与概率模型，发现尽管群体层面的语言偏见微小，但同一事实的投诉因写作风格不同而在2.6-6.3%的情况下获得不同的金钱救济，揭示了决策系统中的语言特征画像与任意性问题。
en_tdlr: This study audits LLMs and a probabilistic "System One" model using fact-preserving sociolinguistic rewrites of consumer complaints, finding that while group-level linguistic bias is small, the same complaint written in different styles receives different monetary remedy decisions 2.6-6.3% of the time, revealing linguistic profiling and arbitrariness in remedy decisions.
